🎃 When to plant pumpkin in Nigeria

Also called Elegede (Yoruba) and Kabewa (Hausa).

Quick answer: Plant pumpkin in Nigeria from April to June and harvest from August to October. Sown at the start of the rains; fruits mature in 3–4 months.

PlantApril to June
HarvestAugust to October
Grows inAll regions
TypeFruit vegetables
Local namesElegede · Kabewa
JanFebMarAprMayJunJulAugSepOctNovDec

■ plant   ■ harvest

About pumpkin

Both the fruit and the young leaves of pumpkin are eaten in Nigeria.

How to plant pumpkin well

Harvest when the skin hardens and the stem dries.

Sown at the start of the rains; fruits mature in 3–4 months.

Diseases and pests of pumpkin

  • Powdery mildewSpace plants and remove badly infected leaves.
  • Fruit fliesBag young fruits or use traps.

Best states for pumpkin

Kano · Kaduna · Benue · Plateau · Oyo · Bauchi

Questions farmers ask

When is the best time to plant pumpkin in Nigeria?

Plant pumpkin in Nigeria from April to June and harvest from August to October. Sown at the start of the rains; fruits mature in 3–4 months.

What is pumpkin called in Yoruba, Hausa and Igbo?

Pumpkin is called Elegede (Yoruba) and Kabewa (Hausa).

When is pumpkin harvested in Nigeria?

Pumpkin is usually harvested from August to October.

Which Nigerian states grow the most pumpkin?

Kano, Kaduna, Benue, Plateau, Oyo and Bauchi are among the best-known pumpkin states.

Can I grow pumpkin in my part of Nigeria?

Yes. Pumpkin grows in every region of Nigeria: North and South.

What diseases attack pumpkin and how do I prevent them?

Powdery mildew: Space plants and remove badly infected leaves. Fruit flies: Bag young fruits or use traps.
